title: Canonical Invariant Violation Event Contract
description: Authoritative schema for recording any breach of a system law. This schema binds detection → logging → escalation → shutdown into a single, governed artifact. Every invariant violation in the system must conform to this schema. Constitutional law enforcement, not logging convenience.

schema_version.description: Semantic version of violation schema. Breaking changes require version bump. Backward compatible only.

violation_id.description: Globally unique identifier (UUID or SHA-256 hash). Used for deduplication, cross-system correlation, and audit trails. MUST be unique across all time.

timestamp.description: Unix epoch seconds (float allowed for sub-second precision) at detection time. Captured immediately when violation is detected.

invariant.description: Canonical invariant identifier that was violated. Must map to invariants defined in state_transition.schema.json, error_taxonomy.schema.json, or platform_policy.schema.json.

domain.description: Scope of violation for routing and escalation. Used by kill switches and alerting systems to determine response scope.

severity.description: Ordered severity level. Directly gates kill switches. CRITICAL always triggers immediate action. Severity ordering: LOW < MEDIUM < HIGH < CRITICAL.

source.description: Where the violation was detected. Mandatory for traceability and debugging.

component.description: Component name that detected violation (e.g., posting_state_store, reconciliation, anomaly_detector)

file.description: Source file where violation was detected (relative path from repository root)

function.description: Function or method name where violation was detected

context.description: Structured snapshot of relevant state at violation time. Never raw dumps. Only relevant fields that explain the violation. Must be JSON-serializable.

intent_id.description: Intent ID if violation relates to specific intent

account_id.description: Account ID if violation relates to specific account

platform.description: Platform name if violation relates to specific platform

current_state.description: Current state value that violated invariant

attempted_state.description: State that was attempted (for transition violations)

error_category.description: Error category if violation relates to error taxonomy

current_value.description: Current value that violated constraint (type varies by violation)

allowed_value.description: Allowed value for constraint (type varies by violation)

impact.description: Impact assessment for triage and escalation. Required for all violations.

affected_intents.description: Number of intents affected by this violation. 0 if no specific intents affected.

affected_accounts.description: List of affected account IDs. Empty array if no specific accounts affected.

data_corruption_risk.description: Whether this violation indicates data corruption is possible or has occurred. CRITICAL if true.

external_exposure.description: Whether violation has exposed or could expose data to external systems or users. HIGH or CRITICAL if true.

system_wide.description: Whether violation affects entire system rather than specific intents/accounts. Automatically true if domain is 'global'.

irreversible.description: Whether violation has caused irreversible state changes. CRITICAL if true.

recommended_action.description: Declarative remediation guidance consumed by kill_switches.py. Determines automatic system response.

metadata.description: Annotations only. Ignored by enforcement logic. Used for operational context and debugging.

correlation_id.description: Correlation ID for tracing across services

operator.description: Operator or automated system that created this violation record

detection_method.description: Method by which violation was detected

related_violation_ids.description: IDs of related violations (e.g., cascading violations)

stack_trace.description: Stack trace if available (truncated to reasonable length)

invariant_catalog.description: Complete catalog of known invariants mapped to their domains and default severities. These invariants are defined in state_transition.schema.json, error_taxonomy.schema.json, and platform_policy.schema.json.

enforcement_matrix.description: Components and their roles in violation handling. No component may swallow violations.

severity_action_mapping.description: Mapping from severity to default actions if recommended_action not specified

failure_semantics.description: What happens when violation cannot be serialized or persisted. Silence is not permitted.

description.const: If a violation cannot be serialized: System enters safe mode, Dispatcher halts, Audit entry forced
If violation cannot be persisted: Retry with exponential backoff, If all retries fail: Halt dispatcher, Force emergency audit entry

validation_rules.description: Additional validation rules beyond JSON schema

rule.const: If data_corruption_risk=true OR external_exposure=true, severity MUST be HIGH or CRITICAL

rule2.const: If domain=global, impact.system_wide MUST be true

rule3.const: If recommended_action=emergency_shutdown, severity MUST be CRITICAL

rule4.const: If recommended_action=halt_dispatcher, severity MUST be HIGH or CRITICAL

rule.const: invariant MUST map to a known invariant from state_transition, error_taxonomy, or platform_policy schemas

rule2.const: domain MUST match the domain of the invariant definition

rule.const: timestamp MUST be within reasonable bounds (not future beyond clock skew, not ancient)
violation_id MUST be globally unique. Duplicate IDs indicate system corruption.

example_violations.description: Canonical examples of properly formatted violations for each violation type. Use these as templates.
